name: Niural AI
summary: Payroll, benefits, HR, PEO and global hiring from one vendor, and — rare in this category — every product carries a published price. Every tier is demo-led with no self-serve sign-up, and the pricing page asks your headcount band before it shows a ladder.
best_for: US companies that want payroll, benefits, PEO and international hiring from one vendor and want to see a number before the call — and especially teams above about fifty people, where the $100 platform fee stops distorting the per-employee rate
skip_if: you are under about ten employees, because the $100 platform fee doubles the effective per-head cost at that size; you need to buy without talking to anyone, since every tier is demo-led; or you only need global payroll for entities you already run, where the $29 tier is the only part of this catalogue you should be pricing
honest_knock:
Every tier says Book a demo. The prices are published — which in payroll is genuinely rare and worth crediting — but there is no self-serve sign-up anywhere on the page, so the published figure is the opening of a conversation rather than something you can act on. Expect the real number to arrive by quote, and expect it to depend on the company-size step you selected before you ever saw a price.

The page changes under you, and that is easy to miss. It asks your headcount band first and adjusts the ladder to match, so two people comparing Niural can honestly quote each other different numbers. Note which band you read when you write the figure down.

The platform fee is the part that decides whether this is cheap. US Payroll is $100 a month before anyone is paid, plus $20 a head. At five employees that is $200 a month, or $40 an employee — double the headline rate. At twenty-five it is $600, or $24 each. At a hundred it is $2,100, or $21 each. The per-employee price you are quoted only becomes the price you pay somewhere north of fifty people, and small teams are the ones most likely to read $20 and budget $20.

The naming needs care too. Contractor of Record and Employer of Record are both $299 per employee a month and they are not the same product: the first keeps the worker a contractor while Niural carries the misclassification risk, the second makes Niural the legal employer in 150-plus countries. Buying the wrong one is an expensive mistake that the identical price does nothing to prevent.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month platform fee plus $20 per employee a month
pricing.notes: (read 18 September 2026 in a live browser on niural.com/pricing) Eight products, each priced separately, and unusually for this category every one of them carries a published figure. US Payroll Standard is $100 a month as a platform fee plus $20 per employee a month, covering multi-state payroll with W-2s and 1099s, unlimited pay schedules and payroll runs, PTO and leave policies, workforce analytics, same-day deposits, full benefits administration with 401(k) and brokered health, dental and vision, and CRM and ATS integrations; US Payroll Enterprise is custom. On the PEO side, PEO Basic starts at $59 per employee a month without benefits, and PEO Plus at $120 with them — adding benefits enrolment, life and disability cover, 401(k), commuter benefits, medical, dental and vision, and HSA, FSA, COBRA and HRA accounts, with terms noted for groups under five employees. Internationally: Contractor Management is $49 per contractor a month, Contractor of Record (branded Niural Armor) is $299 per employee a month, Employer of Record starts at $299 per employee a month across 150-plus countries, and Global Payroll for entities you already own starts at $29 per employee a month. One caveat about reading this page: it asks your company size first (under 25, 25 to 50, 50 to 100, or more than 100) and adjusts what it shows, so the figures above are the under-25 view and a re-read should select the same step.

compare_with.name: Deel, ADP
compare_with.why:
Deel is the closest thing to a mirror we carry, and the two ladders line up product by product (Deel re-verified 17 August 2026). Contractor management: $49 a contractor at both, identical. Contractor of Record: Deel $325, Niural $299. US PEO: Deel from $125, Niural's PEO Plus from $120. And Employer of Record, where the gap is the story: Deel starts at $599 per employee a month, Niural at $299. On published starting prices Niural is half the cost of the best-known name in the category for the most expensive thing either of them sells. That is worth a quote even if you end up elsewhere — and worth asking both what the figure covers, because an EOR price is a floor that country and salary move.

ADP is the counterexample on transparency rather than on price. From our dossier (read 15 August 2026): no public pricing for RUN anywhere on its site, /pricing returns a 404, the product page offers only a Get Pricing button, and the package-comparison page lists all four tiers with Get pricing under each and not one figure. Against that, Niural publishing eight products with numbers attached is the more useful page even though both end in a sales call.
